disease_label_per_paper: Strongyloides hyper-infection leading to fatal acute respiratory distress syndrome

demographics.country_or_region_context: Nigerian man living in the United States for about one year

presentation_summary: A 70-year-old Nigerian man had remote endemic exposure context and was treated for autoimmune necrotizing myopathy with prednisone, methotrexate, and IVIG for about three months.
Before steroid exposure he had marked myopathy, weight loss, AST 266 U/L, ALT 234 U/L, CPK 8497 U/L, hemoglobin 10 g/dL, and eosinophilia 10%.
He was readmitted with lethargy, inability to speak or follow commands, dry cough, occasional fever, diarrhea, and deterioration while still taking immunosuppressive therapy.

Admission findings included fever 39.3 degC, BP 109/56 mmHg, tachypnea, tachycardia, crackles with reduced basal breath sounds, oral thrush, sodium 122 mmol/L, hemoglobin 8 g/dL, leukopenia with eosinophilia, lactate 4.5 mmol/L, and bilateral infiltrates.

On hospital day 2 he developed severe hypoxemia and cardiac arrest requiring intubation; CT chest showed dense bilateral consolidation and ground-glass opacities with PaO2/FiO2 96 and no pulmonary embolism.
BAL grew Strongyloides stercoralis larvae, the second stool sample showed rhabditiform larvae, Strongyloides serology and HIV testing were negative, and blood cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Steroids were stopped and ivermectin plus albendazole were started with antibiotics and ARDS care, but he died on hospital day 19.

quality_warnings: BAL and stool larvae are confirmatory microbiology and are marked use_in_ranking false where duplicated in course observations.
The paper reports ivermectin as 200 mg/kg; the case preserves the source wording in treatment text rather than correcting it in structured dosing.
Initial WBC count was not provided, so eosinophilia at readmission is encoded qualitatively and the earlier 10% eosinophilia is preserved as a fraction.
Respiratory-rate and heart-rate numeric values were not reported at readmission; tachypnea and tachycardia are preserved as narrative evidence rather than invented measurements.
